subject: ophthalmology
title: Neural Crest Derivatives and Optic Cup

steps.tx: **Neural crest derivatives** in the eye include corneal stroma and endothelium, trabecular meshwork, iris stroma, ciliary muscle and uveal melanocytes, migrated from crest mesenchyme around the optic cup. Their shared origin explains anterior segment dysgenesis syndromes where cornea, angle and iris fail together. Crest failure also links ocular signs to systemic neurocristopathies in syndromic children.
steps.say: Corneal stroma together with meshwork, iris stroma and melanocytes is derived from neural crest embryologically. Shared crest origin therefore gives explanation of combined anterior segment failure in dysgenesis syndromes. Systemic crest signs are company for ocular disease in syndromic children.

steps.tx: The **optic cup** is neuroectoderm doubled on itself, outer layer becoming pigment epithelium and inner layer neural retina, with ciliary and iris epithelia as its anterior continuations. The cup cavity collapses as layers appose, failure leaving congenital retinal detachment configurations. Optic fissure closure failure inferiorly produces typical coloboma of iris, ciliary body, retina and disc in one embryological line.
steps.say: Doubled neuroectoderm forms pigment epithelium outside and neural retina inside the cup. Anterior continuations of the cup give ciliary and iris epithelia. Inferior fissure failure produces the typical coloboma line.

steps.tx: **Optic cup** invagination begins when optic vesicle contacts lens placode, each inducing the other in reciprocal embryological signalling. Vesicle without cup gives microphthalmia pathways, while fissure persistence gives colobomatous microphthalmia spectra. Clinical coloboma is always inferonasal because the fissure lies inferiorly during closure, a location rule that separates typical from atypical defects at fundus examination.
steps.say: Reciprocal induction couples lens placode and optic cup formation during embryology together. Inferior fissure position makes typical coloboma inferonasal at fundus examination. Location therefore separates typical defects from atypical defects.

steps.tx: Corneal transparency depends on crest derived stromal lamellae regularity and endothelial pump keeping stroma deturgesced, both crest products. Endothelial cells barely regenerate in adults, so counts fall with age, surgery and Fuchs dystrophy until oedema clouds vision. **Specular microscopy** counts this crest monolayer preoperatively, linking embryology to cataract surgical safety assessment.
steps.say: Crest derived stroma together with endothelium maintains corneal transparency throughout adult life. Non regenerating endothelium declines with age, surgery and dystrophy progressively. Preoperative cell counting therefore guides cataract surgical safety.

steps.tx: Axenfeld Rieger and Peters spectra pattern crest migration and vesicle separation together, giving posterior embryotoxon, iris strands, corectopia and glaucoma from angle dysgenesis. Glaucoma in anterior segment dysgenesis is therefore developmental outflow failure, treated by angle or filtration logic from the outflow lesson. **Angle dysgenesis** in a child with iris anomalies should always trigger pressure measurement, not observation alone.
steps.say: Crest patterning failure gives iris anomalies together with developmental glaucoma from birth onward. Angle dysgenesis gives outflow failure that needs pressure measurement always in childhood. Iris anomaly in childhood therefore needs glaucoma assessment without delay.

steps.tx: Uveal melanocytes from crest explain congenital melanocytosis and naevus distribution, while iris pigment epithelium from cup explains why pupil margin pigment belongs to neuroectoderm. Two pigment systems in one iris is a favourite examination discrimination. **Heterochromia** workup separates crest melanocyte failure in Waardenburg patterns from acquired sympathetic or inflammatory causes by onset and company kept.
steps.say: Two pigment systems together are present in one iris from entirely different embryological layers. Crest melanocytes in stroma are different from cup pigment epithelium at the margin. Onset and company give separation of congenital heterochromia from acquired causes.

steps.tx: Sclera and choroidal stroma blend crest with mesoderm contributions regionally, which is why simple three layer derivative tables vary between textbooks at margins. Examinations reward core certainties, lens surface, retina cup, cornea stroma crest, over contested boundaries. **Core mapping** should be answered confidently and marginal structures qualified rather than guessed as absolutes.
steps.say: Marginal ocular structures have a blend of crest together with mesoderm contributions regionally in development. Core derivative certainties therefore deserve confident answers during examinations in this subject. Contested boundaries need qualification rather than absolute guessing.

steps.tx: Crest and cup together predict coloboma company: inferior iris defect travels with ciliary, retinal and disc defects along the fissure, while isolated lid coloboma stays surface ectoderm. Finding one fissure defect therefore mandates dilated fundus examination for its deeper companions. **Visual prognosis** follows macular and disc involvement, not iris appearance, however dramatic the keyhole pupil looks externally.
steps.say: Inferior iris defects together have deeper fissure companions along the closure line predictably. Dilated fundus examination is therefore mandatory after any fissure defect is found. Visual prognosis is based on macular and disc involvement mainly.

cards.b: Corneal stroma and endothelium, trabecular meshwork, iris stroma, ciliary muscle, uveal melanocytes.
Inferonasal, along inferior optic fissure closure line, involving iris to disc in one line.
Crest melanocytes in stroma plus cup neuroectoderm pigment epithelium at pupil margin.

keys: Cup gives retina, crest gives anterior segment framework
Inferior defect means examine the whole fissure line
Dysgenesis glaucoma is developmental outflow failure
